newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds fall back, 10-year bund gap narrows.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds fall back, 10-year bund gap narrows.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped in a quiet summer holiday market on Monday, with the 10-year bond yield gap with Germany narrowing and dealers seeing the same general trend continuing up to the close.
"The Danish bond market has done pretty well so far. We have been unaffected by profit-taking in the German September bund. Market players are holding a low profile," one dealer said.

The tone setting eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.28 point from the opening at 113.94, with yield at 5.88 percent while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark dipped 0.29 point to 106.73, yielding 6.09 percent.
Turnover in the 2006 and 2007 bonds was around 450 million and 660 million crowns respectively.
The 2006's September future rose 0.36 point to 113.54 with 13 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 was unaltered at 92.20.
The crown traded at an almost static 3.8094 per mark at 1110 gmt.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed three basis points to 51.
